enabled.hint: Master switch for interjections, proactive chat and schedules; groups cannot override it. Start with one test session. Interjections also require AstrBot's built-in active reply to be disabled.
Global interjection default. Groups may inherit, enable or disable it, but the master switch must be on for all sessions.

threshold.hint: 0–1. The final score must be strictly greater; equality does not trigger. Lower is easier to trigger. 0.7 is a score, not a 70% probability. Zero energy does not necessarily prevent interjections.

debounce_seconds.hint: Wait this long after the last group message before judging, avoiding a model request per message. Continuous chat is capped by Maximum merge time.

cooldown_seconds.hint: After a confirmed bot send in this session, wait at least this long before another interjection or proactive chat. Normal mentions are unrestricted. 0 means no wait.

max_recent_messages.hint: Limits activity, energy and deduplication records, not chat references. Group reference count follows AstrBot's maximum injected group messages and is not cleared by the activity window.

weights.hint: Weights represent importance and need not sum to 1. Positive scores normally, negative reverses the factor, 0 excludes it. At least one must be nonzero.

model.hint: Positive favors higher model scores; negative favors lower model scores.

activity.hint: More and more recent messages from other accounts increase activity. Positive favors busy conversations; negative reverses this. Other accounts are not classified as humans or bots.

energy.hint: Fewer recent bot sends mean more energy. Positive reduces consecutive interjections; negative reverses it. Energy is a score factor, not a mute switch.

window_seconds.hint: Counts other accounts' messages in this session during this window. 600 seconds means 10 minutes.

target_messages.hint: Reaching this count fills the message-count component. The final activity score also decreases as the conversation becomes quiet.

freshness_seconds.hint: Activity declines with time since another account's last message and reaches zero after this duration. New messages recalculate it.

window_seconds.hint: Counts recent bot sends in this window. 3600 seconds means one hour. Ordinary replies observed through AstrBot count too.

target_messages.hint: This many confirmed sends in the window reduce energy to zero. Larger values reduce energy more slowly. A zero-energy score may still pass the final threshold.

decision.hint: Judges interjection suitability only. The original agent writes replies. LLM uses an existing chat model; Jev uses a dedicated endpoint. Groups may choose different modes; both can be configured.

mode.hint: llm uses a configured AstrBot chat model; jev uses a dedicated Jev model. This sets the global default; groups may choose another. Unused modes do not send requests.

provider_id.hint: Required for llm mode. Select an existing AstrBot chat provider for judgment only; the session's original model generates replies.

prompt.hint: Tell the model when the bot should join. Keep defaults if unsure. Supports {persona_prompt}, {conversation_history}, {recent_messages}, {activity_score}, {energy_score} and other placeholders.

timeout_seconds.hint: Maximum request time including retries and retry waits. Timeout skips this interjection. Queue time is included separately in Judgment validity.

jev_endpoint.hint: Full HTTPS URL compatible with TypeSafe /systemone; no path is appended. API key and selected references are sent there. HTTP is allowed only for localhost/loopback. No credentials, query parameters or fragments in the URL; enter credentials in the key field.

jev_api_key.hint: Required for jev mode, supplied by your Jev service. Used on the server only and not logged. Do not share it.

jev_model.hint: A model supported by the endpoint; default jev-latest. For proxies, use a model name supported by that service.

jev_state_template.hint: Extra background for judgment. Current input, selected history, group messages and existing image descriptions are appended automatically. History placeholders are usually unnecessary and may duplicate data. This does not modify the reply agent.

retry_attempts.hint: Additional attempts after the first failure; 0 disables retries. Only connection errors, rate limits and temporary service errors retry, not invalid formats/keys. All retries share the request timeout.

retry_delay_seconds.hint: Wait before the first retry; later waits increase. Server retry-after guidance takes priority within the judgment timeout.

debounce_max_seconds.hint: Maximum wait from the first message in a batch. Prevents continuous chat from postponing judgment forever. Cannot be shorter than Pause wait.

decision_max_age_seconds.hint: Starts when judgment references are prepared, including queue and request time. Stale results are discarded. Ordinary messages do not cancel running judgments; normal activation or a conversation-branch change invalidates them.

activation_prompts.hint: Controls how the bot joins after a judgment, not whether to join. One variant is chosen randomly and may repeat. History, names and reasons are reference data, not system instructions.

timezone.hint: Timezone for routine, schedule dates and daily counters, e.g. Asia/Shanghai. Enter an IANA timezone name, not a translated city name.

sleep_hours.hint: Pauses both features; normal mentions and native future tasks remain available. Comma-separated ranges, e.g. 23:00-07:00,12:00-13:00. Start is inclusive, end exclusive; equal endpoints mean all day. Global blank means no sleep period. Sleep overrides active periods.

active_hours.hint: Only these periods allow proactive chat; interjections are also allowed. Other waking periods allow interjections only. Comma-separated ranges, e.g. 12:00-13:00,19:00-22:00. Cross-midnight supported; equal endpoints mean all day. Sleep takes priority. Blank means no proactive periods.

enabled.hint: Global proactive default. Groups may inherit, enable or disable it; the master switch must be on for all sessions.

daily_limit.description: Daily proactive attempt quota per session
daily_limit.hint: Integer 1–1000. Opportunities are distributed across active time with a random time in each part. A sent or normally completed silent run counts once. Failed, missed or restricted opportunities are not replaced. A new plan is prepared next day. Some or all attempts may choose silence.

prompts.hint: Guide the opening and tone. One variant is chosen randomly and may repeat. {routine_state} is sleeping/normal/active, not emotion. Proactive runs have no real sender. {user_last_message_time_ago} and {unreplied_count} describe recent interaction.

task_prompt.hint: Tell the bot what to do on this opportunity, alongside the style prompts above. Prompts cannot override current-session scope or the requirement to use the send tool.

context.hint: Group message count follows AstrBot's maximum injected group messages. Persistent history is preferred; read-only pending context and temporary plugin messages are fallbacks. Newer messages are retained when trimming. See replay for sources/counts. Framework data is never consumed, cleared or rewritten.

history_messages.hint: Last N saved messages in the current branch, not N question-answer pairs. 0 initially selects all, then character/token budgets trim them. Only judgment references are limited; native history and agent context are unchanged.

judgment_max_tokens.hint: Tokens estimate model input length, not character count or billing usage. Includes prompts and references. Older records are removed first; if still over budget, judgment is skipped. Leave room for service limits.

judgment_max_chars.hint: Applied alongside the token budget. Each character, letter or punctuation counts once. Limits this judgment input without changing native history.

message_max_chars.hint: Overlong records retain their beginning and are marked shortened. Media files retain type labels and existing image descriptions rather than encoded content.

reuse_image_descriptions.hint: Adds existing AstrBot group-image descriptions without re-analyzing images or consuming framework records. Descriptions already present in history/group messages are unaffected. Missing image content is never guessed.

runtime.hint: Shared concurrency limits and an optional extra proactive whole-run timeout. Blank uses AstrBot's model/tool limits. Judgment request timeout is separate.

judgment_concurrency.hint: Maximum judgment requests across all sessions. Positive integer; not a per-group interjection rate. Larger values may increase provider load.

proactive_concurrency.hint: Maximum proactive runs across all sessions. Other runs queue at capacity. Daily quota per session is unchanged.

proactive_timeout_seconds.description: Extra proactive whole-run timeout (seconds; blank uses AstrBot)
proactive_timeout_seconds.hint: Blank adds no plugin whole-run deadline; model retries, fallbacks and tools use AstrBot limits, which are not one unified timeout. A positive integer limits execution from acquiring a proactive slot through history save, including session lock, context, models, tools and sending; slot-queue time is excluded. Already sent content cannot be retracted.

diagnostics.hint: Temporary execution steps and request text may contain chat content. Known credentials and encoded media are hidden. In-memory only, bounded by retention, capacity and per-step length.

retention_minutes.hint: Finished records age from completion; others from creation. Active proactive runs are not expired by this timer. Capacity limits may remove their step history, but current progress stays available.

max_memory_mb.hint: Estimated size limit for temporary steps; old history is removed at capacity. Active run summaries are retained separately. 1 MiB is 1024×1024 bytes. This is not a total plugin/AstrBot memory limit.

max_step_chars.hint: Limits console display text only, not what the model actually receives. Shortened text is marked.

session_groups.hint: No groups means all supported known sessions. Adding any group limits interjections/proactive chat to listed sessions. Outside-scope schedules have a separate switch. Group schedule limits use inherit for global defaults; blank means unlimited. Most other blank group fields inherit.

sids.hint: One group/private SID per item. An admin can send /active_status in the target session and copy its full SID, e.g. connection:GroupMessage:group_id. Groups share settings, not history. Duplicates within a group are merged; cross-group duplicates or invalid IDs pause autonomous speech and show the field location.

interjection_mode.hint: Follow global uses the global interjection switch. Enabled/Disabled overrides that feature only. All choices require the master switch and scope/model/threshold/framework permissions.

proactive_mode.hint: Follow global uses the global proactive switch. Enabled/Disabled overrides that feature only. All choices require the master switch and scope/routine/quota/framework permissions.

agenda_id.hint: Internal association maintained automatically. No need to inspect or enter it. Renaming a group does not change the association.

agenda_preview_days.hint: inherit follows global; a number overrides it. Blank means unlimited for this group. 0 disables automatic context; tools and pause rules remain available.

agenda_exclusions.description: Global schedules excluded by this group

agenda.hint: Schedule feature settings. Edit actual records in Console → Routine and schedules. Schedules provide context, not timed reminders; use native future tasks for reminders.

enabled.hint: Provides applicable schedule context and query/management tools, and applies pause rules. Can be enabled independently under the master switch. Preview 0 disables injection only; tools and pause rules still work.

outside_scope.description: Provide global schedules outside plugin scope
outside_scope.hint: Outside-scope sessions can receive global/shared and targeted schedules, query them and manage their own exclusive records. Does not enable interjections or proactive chat. Also allows target SIDs in the global schedule editor.

background_description.hint: Global only; shared by all sessions. Blank/whitespace restores the default description. Schedule JSON is appended automatically.

preview_days.hint: Default 7 days. Blank means unlimited future range; 0 disables the automatic description/JSON, while schedule tools remain available. Repeats contribute their next occurrence only.

max_items.hint: Blank is unlimited. A positive integer limits ongoing and upcoming context items separately. Tool queries are not limited by this setting.

events.hint: Records live in agenda.json in the plugin data directory. Edit global, group and targeted schedules in the console. Up to 100 shared global rules, 100 per group/SID and 1000 total.

id.hint: Generated and maintained by the plugin. No need to enter or inspect it; renaming a schedule keeps its ID.

title.hint: For example: lunch break, reading or group activity. At most 80 characters.

description.hint: Explain who is doing what and when, e.g. the bot's lunch break or a group dinner. Used as reply context, not a reminder or proof of completion. Optional; max 1000 characters.

start_date.hint: YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. 2026-10-20. Repeating schedules take effect from this day.

until.hint: Repeating rules only. Blank means no cutoff. A date such as 2026-12-31 still allows an occurrence to start that day and finish after midnight.

time_mode.hint: All day covers the whole day. A time range covers the specified hours; an earlier end crosses midnight. Equal times should use All day. Cron uses its expression and duration instead.

start_time.hint: 24-hour time, e.g. 09:00. Ordinary time-range rules only; unused for all-day/Cron.

end_time.hint: 24-hour time, e.g. 18:00. Earlier than start means next day. Unused for all-day/Cron.

repeat.hint: Once runs only on the start date. Daily, weekly and yearly repeat accordingly; Cron uses an expression. Weekly supports multiple days. Holidays and adjusted workdays are not inferred.

weekdays.hint: Choose one or more days of the week. Used for weekly schedules only.

cron.hint: Cron only; choose daily/weekly if unfamiliar. Five fields: minute hour day month weekday. 0 9 * * * means daily 09:00. Sunday is 0 or 7; mon-fri also works. Day and weekday restrictions must both match. No timed reminders are created.

cron_duration_minutes.hint: Cron only; 1–1440. A daily 09:00 start with 60-minute duration is active 09:00–10:00.

pause_interjection.hint: Pauses automatic interjections while the event is active. Normal mentions, commands and native future tasks are unaffected. Schedules must be enabled.

pause_proactive.hint: Pauses proactive chat while the event is active. Normal mentions, commands and native future tasks are unaffected. Schedules must be enabled.

group_id.hint: Choose global or a session group. A missing group must be relinked; its schedule never becomes global automatically.

target_sids.hint: Blank uses the global/group scope above. Full SIDs make this exclusive to those sessions instead of inheriting group scope.

tools.query_description: Read schedules visible in the CURRENT conversation; this tool never changes data. Use range (default) for current/future occurrences, or supply dates to read the past. Each rule appears once: the FIRST occurrence overlapping the requested range, with its repeat rule. status describes that occurrence, not whether the whole recurring rule has ended. Use catalog to list all visible rules, including disabled ones, before editing. To edit/delete, copy id and revision from this result into manage_schedule. Only editable=true rules can be changed. Shared global/group rules are read-only. Schedules are background context, NOT timed reminders.
tools.manage_description: Manage schedules belonging ONLY to the CURRENT conversation. Never accepts a target SID. create: pass action=create and a nonempty events array; omit id/revision/changes. update: query_schedule first, then pass action=update, exact id, revision, and changes containing ONLY fields to change. delete: query first, then pass action=delete, exact id and revision; omit events/changes. Only editable=true records can be updated/deleted. Global/group/multi-session rules are read-only. Updating/deleting a repeating rule affects the ENTIRE series, not one occurrence. Dates use the current conversation timezone. No reminders are created. Omit unused optional fields; do not use null. Report success ONLY when saved=true. Examples: {"action":"create","events":[{"title":"Reading","start_date":"2026-10-20"}]}; {"action":"update","id":"<from query>","revision":"<from query>","changes":{"title":"New title"}}; {"action":"delete","id":"<from query>","revision":"<from query>"}.

mode.description: range (default): first occurrence per rule in the date range. catalog: all visible rules, including disabled; dates are ignored.

start_date.description: Optional YYYY-MM-DD, including past dates. Defaults to now. Supplying only a past end date queries up to that day.

end_date.description: Optional YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive, including past dates. Blank means no end limit. One occurrence per rule in the range.

create_fields.events: Required nonempty array of schedule objects, e.g. [{"title":"Reading","start_date":"2026-10-20"}]. The whole batch is validated before saving.
create_fields.title: Required nonempty title, at most 80 characters.
create_fields.description: Optional description, at most 1000 characters. Omit for none.
create_fields.start_date: Required start date YYYY-MM-DD, year 1900–2199. Repeats take effect from this day.
create_fields.until: Optional last start date YYYY-MM-DD for repeating events, inclusive. Empty string removes the cutoff.
create_fields.enabled: Optional; defaults to true. false creates a disabled rule.
create_fields.time_mode: Optional; defaults to 全天 (all day). 时段 (time range) requires start_time/end_time. Omit for Cron.
create_fields.start_time: Required for ordinary 时段 rules: HH:MM. Omit for all-day and Cron rules.
create_fields.end_time: Required for ordinary 时段 rules: HH:MM. Earlier than start means next day; cannot equal start. Omit for all-day and Cron.
create_fields.repeat: Optional; defaults to 不重复 (once). 每天=daily, 每周=selected weekdays, 每年=same month/day yearly, Cron=expression.
create_fields.weekdays: Required only for 每周: at least one weekday value, e.g. ["周一","周五"]. Omit otherwise.
create_fields.cron: Required only for Cron: five fields (minute hour day month weekday), e.g. 0 7 * * * for daily 07:00.
create_fields.pause_interjection: Optional; true pauses interjections during the event. Default false.
create_fields.pause_proactive: Optional; true pauses proactive chat during the event. Default false.
